facts.statement: This extinct basal shark, known as Duffin's shark, is represented by a single species found in the Late Triassic of England.
facts.quote: Duffinselache (Duffin's shark) is an extinct genus of basal shark elasmobranchii cartilaginous fish, known from a single species, Duffinselache holwellensis, collected from the Late Triassic (Rhaetian stage) of England.

facts.statement: Duffin first named the animal in 1998, initially classifying it as a species of Polyacrodus.
facts.quote: It was first named by Duffin in 1998 as a species of Polyacrodus.

facts.statement: In 2012, researchers Plamen S. Andreev and Gilles Cuny moved the species to a new genus, designating it the type species of Duffinselache.
facts.quote: Plamen S. Andreev and Gilles Cuny in 2012 reassigned it to a new genus as its type species, Polyacrodus holwellensis.

facts.statement: Duffinselache belongs to the class Chondrichthyes and the parent group Neoselachii.
The animal lived during the Rhaetian stage, between 205.7 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Rhaetian (205.7 to 201.4 million years ago)
